why: Record 0060 reported red mutations without binding their evidence. A narrative does not replace the ordered proof, so each of the five failure models named in record 0059 is reproduced here: the exact mutation, the smallest detector that sees it, the expected and the actual result, and the source hash before and after, which must be identical. No test was adapted to any mutant.
rule: A correction is not closed while removing it leaves every test green.

mutants.failureModel: physical disposal begins while a lease is still held
mutants.mutation: Invalidate schedules the disposal unconditionally instead of only when no lease is active.
mutants.actual: Fehler!      : Fehler:     2, erfolgreich:     0, übersprungen:     0, gesamt:     2, Dauer: 73 ms
mutants.note: The first attempt at this mutant stayed green: the spec checked probe.Started.IsCompleted after a single await Task.Yield(), which races the queued disposal and passes whatever the implementation does. The spec was strengthened to wait a short bounded time for a signal that must never arrive. The mutant was not weakened and the detector was not adapted to it -- the detector was too weak to see it, and that is itself a finding of this run.

mutants.failureModel: the real Peer/405 cause is replaced by a locally produced 491
mutants.mutation: NotAvailable always builds the local Library/491 answer and discards the broker's stored reason.
mutants.actual: Fehler!      : Fehler:     2, erfolgreich:     0, übersprungen:     0, gesamt:     2, Dauer: 104 ms

mutants.failureModel: a failed connect or request pipe connection is not released
mutants.mutation: WaitForBusEndpoint no longer calls handle.Disconnect() when the wait fails, so a refused connect leaves its registration behind.
mutants.redDetail: the request id was still bound after the first connect failed, so connecting it again was refused by the pipe instead of by the broker: DuplicateKeyPipeConfigurationException

finding: M1 did not turn red on its first attempt, and that is a result of this run rather than a footnote. The detector checked probe.Started.IsCompleted after a single await Task.Yield(); the disposal is queued to the thread pool, so the check raced it and would have passed whatever the implementation did. The detector was strengthened -- it now waits a short bounded time for a signal that must never arrive -- and the mutant was left exactly as it was. The class comment claiming that nothing here waits for a duration was corrected at the same time, because it no longer described the code.
reproduction: python3 tools/ci/policy_validator.py and dotnet test --filter FullyQualifiedName~RabbitMqTransport.UnitTests reproduce M1..M4 without a broker; M5 needs the pinned fixture.
